skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/orchestrate.why: The orch CLI is excluded and the verification ledger lives in GitHub: every orch command becomes a direct store-file edit or a ledger comment on the PR, the store moves to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/, and restacks and cloud-only spawns become background agents with worktree isolation. The orch frontier command's empty-gt guard becomes an instruction. Worktree agents share one repository, so workers release their branches and the stacker frees held branches before a restack. Every agent runs on this machine, so the isolation exception covers only the coordinator's own working tree and worktree agents may read the store. The different-family verifier resolves to the models document's verifier and verifier-diff-audit roles, with a fallback line when there is no second family.

Roles: the Subagents defaults resolve from docs/agents/models.md (written by setup-milliways) instead of setup-pstack and Cursor model slugs. Leaf skills: says where principle leaves and this skill's own files live (<milliways>), since Claude Code does not list skills with model invocation off.

skills/pr/SKILL.md.why: PR anatomy: keeps Summary, Evidence and Merge Danger, and adds a conventional-commit title, a calldiff call-tree summary sanity-checked for dynamic dispatch (Mermaid as fallback), a scope line, before/after media attached with gh --attach, the red-then-green test, a Blast radius: high|medium|low line with the one fact it is safe because of, the door:one-way label, commits regrouped in dependency order, the verifier verdict at the head SHA with its tier label, a decision-log link and the Fix-forward: #N line, which the trust-ladder scorer reads. One concern per PR, no stacks. Adds the Prototype PRs variant: a draft titled prototype: with a screencast per variant, closed unmerged with the chef's pick recorded on the PR and the ticket.

skills/reflect/SKILL.md.why: Step 1 hard-codes Cursor's three transcript layouts and its JSONL record shape; Claude Code has a session and a subagent layout, and its first user event carries the prompt.
